title: AI Search Audit
description: Turned a founder's AI-search question into a practical audit: site checks, 74 search-result rows, browser retests, and a private action report.
seoTitle: AI Search Audit Case Study | Health Services Startup
seoDescription: A case study draft on an AI-search audit for a health-services startup, covering public-site checks, 74 search-result rows, browser retests, evidence files, and a private action report.
role: Solo product engineer and audit lead
constraints: The audit used public information only: no private search dashboard, analytics account, website admin, or server access.
The live website could not be changed during the audit, so the report had to give clear next steps for the founder or website helper.
The work involved a health-services business, so the public case study avoids private details and does not overstate medical, ranking, or sales outcomes.
The first useful version needed to be ready before a follow-up conversation; the final evidence files are complete, and the private report is separate from the public case study.
problem: A founder wanted to understand how a health-services business could show up when people ask AI tools about at-home blood testing and related services.
The audit needed to show what AI tools could already find, which public pages or sources were helping, where the business was missing, and what could be fixed.
There was limited time before an in-person follow-up, so the work had to become a clear report instead of a loose list of generic AI-search tips.
solution: Reviewed the public website, separate blog, site maps, search access rules, visible page text, headings, and page labels before turning recommendations into clear next steps.
Ran Spanish and English AI-search tests for obvious and non-obvious questions, then separated live answer notes from the reusable testing plan.
Created early checklist and diagnostic PDFs, finalized the evidence files, then moved the work into a private report site with source notes, results, action cards, and a monthly retest plan.
result: Converted an open-ended AI-search question into a clear audit package with website checks, search tests, grouped findings, action cards, and a finalized 74-row evidence file.

Found practical fixes without claiming client impact yet: one missing search-instructions file, uneven business and service labels in page data, useful site maps, readable pages, and city pages with more than one main heading.
Added 12 rows checked in a browser during the final retest and brought browser-checked evidence to 33 rows, covering every earlier to-check item while keeping old manual rows for history.
Built a private report site with first-fix priorities, next improvements, evidence results, a monthly retest plan, appendix material, and 9 action cards.
Kept the outcome honest: the work now proves a repeatable audit system and evidence file, not client impact or a measured increase in AI mentions.
deliveryHighlights: Final evidence file: 74 search-result rows, including 33 checked in the browser and 12 added in the final retest.
Early files include a practical checklist PDF and a longer diagnostic PDF.
Final files include a test-question list, results spreadsheet, source notes, action-card notes, handoff notes, and a private report site.
The private report site is password-gated and hidden from search engines.
